answer: If I would know the answer, I would tell you.
If you had told us earlier, we could have adjusted the schedule.
If I'd have known about the traffic, I would've left earlier.
sense_problem: Option A ('If I'd have known') is a common native-speaker form, so some learners may hear it as fine; defensible as a B2.2 mistake but the task should say it is about standard written English.

answer: If I hadn't stayed up so late, I wouldn't be so tired now.
A quality now caused a result in the past.
instruction_problem: Options are abstract and wordy ('A quality now caused a result in the past'); a learner may not parse them. 'a better memory' is a general trait, not clearly 'now'.
sense_problem: The model sentence is odd: 'If I had a better memory, I would have remembered' is a weak mixed conditional; adult-natural but borderline.

answer: If only I would have saved more money.
sense_problem: Mistake is believable (would have after if only).

answer: He asked me what time was it.
where we should meet
instruction_problem: Unclear how many words to type and whether to start with 'where' (already printed in the quote only). Many correct answers: should/ought to/were to/would, 'they' vs 'we' (pronoun ambiguity), and 'where to meet'. A typed key will miss some.

answer: The driver apologised for blocking the exit.
She accused me of breaking the printer.
The manager apologised for the delay and promised that it would not happen again.
instruction_problem: Only three options, others obviously fail; fine.

answer: how to set up
whether
wrong_options_that_fit: 'if' is accepted by many speakers after 'depends on' in informal English ('depends on if'), though 'whether' is the standard form.
instruction_problem: The learner may argue 'if' is also correct; consider adding 'or not' or a different frame.

answer: whether the project is worth the cost
Whomever wins the contract will celebrate.
sense_problem: Overlaps with 041 (same whoever/whomever idea); 'whomever' is a trap many learners (and natives) overuse, acceptable but rule is formal.

answer: had been walking
wrong_options_that_fit: 'has been walking' does not fit the past 'were sore' (not a good fit); none.

answer: had been working
instruction_problem: 'was working' and 'had worked' are also correct English here; only 'had been working' is clearly best (less natural variants).

answer: had been waiting
she had been working there for ten years when she left
other_correct: when she left, she had been working there for ten years
when she left she had been working there for ten years
she had been working for ten years there when she left (less natural)

answer: owing to
instruction_problem: Distractors 'owing' and 'on account' are fragments of the same phrase, not real alternatives; easy for B2.1.

answer: The shop closed early owing the strike.
Save a copy on a USB stick in case your laptop crashes.
other_correct: Save a copy on a USB stick in case your laptop should crash.
Save a copy on a USB stick in case your laptop were to crash.
Save a copy on a USB stick in case your laptop does crash.
instruction_problem: Several corrections possible (crashes, should crash, were to crash); a typed key must accept them.

answer: Therefore
instruction_problem: Easy for B2.2: the two preposition cards need a noun and 'Whereas' is not causal, so only 'Therefore' fits at a glance.

answer: whether
if
instruction_problem: Second gap: 'whether we're late' without 'or not' is marginal; 'if' is the natural choice. First gap: 'if to expect' is wrong. Third card 'what' is a trivial distractor.
sense_problem: 'know whether to expect us before ten' is slightly awkward.

answer: had she not missed the train, she would be here already
other_correct: had she not missed the train, she would already be here
she would not be here already had she missed the train
had she missed the train, she would not be here already
instruction_problem: No 'More than one answer is possible' note although several correct orders exist; inversion without 'if' also hard to infer.

answer: the agent said I might need a visa
other_correct: I said the agent might need a visa
instruction_problem: Two correct sentences (agent/I swap); too easy for B2.1 (8 cards).

answer: I would tell you the answer if I knew
other_correct: if I knew the answer I would tell you
if I knew I would tell you the answer
I would tell you if I knew the answer
instruction_problem: Many correct orders but no note saying more than one answer is possible.

answer: we would have known about the problem if you had called
other_correct: if you had called we would have known about the problem
if you had called about the problem we would have known
we would have known if you had called about the problem
if we had known about the problem we would have called you
we would have called you if we had known about the problem
instruction_problem: Many correct orders (including a different sentence with 'we had known ... we would have called you'); no note about multiple answers.

answer: would you mind telling me how long the repair will take
other_correct: will you mind telling me how long the repair would take (wrong/unnatural)
instruction_problem: Grammar fine; 'Put in order to make a question' fits.

answer: order
If I had a garden, I would grow vegetables.
other_correct: If I had a garden, I'd grow vegetables.
I would grow vegetables if I had a garden.
I'd grow vegetables if I had a garden.
If I had a garden, I could grow vegetables.
If I had a garden, I might grow vegetables.

answer: Were the price lower, more people would buy it.
other_correct: Were the price to be lower, more people would buy it.
More people would buy it were the price lower.
instruction_problem: Starting word is given and the rest is mostly copying.

answer: If only we had backed up the files, we wouldn't be in this mess now.
If I had charged my phone, it would be working now.
whether the supplier can meet the deadline
instruction_problem: Near duplicate of 014 (same frame 'The question is ___').

answer: we had been hiking for hours when the storm began
other_correct: when the storm began we had been hiking for hours
the storm began when we had been hiking for hours
instruction_problem: Several orders correct; no note about it.

answer: Hadn't she missed the train, she'd be here now.
sense_problem: Option B is a form hardly any learner writes ('Hadn't she'); the mistake is somewhat exotic. Option C is a correct mixed conditional that some may wrongly mark.

answer: She asked me how to start.
sense_problem: Option 'asked to me' is a random preposition error, not a very believable one.

answer: The client complained that the delivery had been three days late.
It remains unclear how we will pay for the repairs.
Whomever gets home first should start dinner.
wrong_options_that_fit: Option B 'Invite whoever you like' is accepted in everyday English (formal 'whomever'); a pedantic learner may mark it wrong.
instruction_problem: Overlaps with 015.

answer: would send
had been waiting
instruction_problem: 'had waited' is also correct; only 'had been waiting' stresses duration.

answer: have
instruction_problem: Several forms fit ('in case you had' is less natural in this context); typed key must accept variants.

answer: visiting
instruction_problem: The gap can hold a whole clause as well as -ing; the verb hint '(visit)' does not say which.

answer: wouldn't be spending
lived
instruction_problem: 'could live' and 'were living' are also correct with '(live)'.

answer: did
instruction_problem: 'should do' is also correct (less common).

answer: to go
instruction_problem: Open gap: many clauses fit; should say 'one word' or give a frame.

answer: of selling
instruction_problem: Gap includes the preposition 'of', which the learner must supply; instruction doesn't say so.

answer: repaired
It's high time you started looking for a new job.
other_correct: It's high time you started to look for a new job.
It's high time you looked for a new job.
It is high time you started looking for a new job.
It's high time you began looking for a new job.
It's high time you started looking for a job.
It's high time that you started looking for a new job.
It's high time to start looking for a new job.
instruction_problem: Many answers; a typed key must be tolerant.

answer: I'd rather you didn't bring your dog to the office.
other_correct: I would rather you didn't bring your dog to the office.
I'd rather you did not bring your dog to the office.
I would rather you did not bring your dog to the office.
I'd rather you not bring your dog to the office.
I'd rather you wouldn't bring your dog to the office.
